facts.label: Readiness view
facts.text: The effective source set is adequate for a credit snapshot with stated limitations, and no consumer is blocked. Seven issuer documents from a single registrant are present: one audited annual report, three quarterly reports and three quarterly earnings releases, covering fiscal 2025 and each quarter of 2026 through 2026-09-30. All are filed statements or issuer releases for MaxLinear, Inc. in USD, with consistent period labels, and the third quarter release agrees with the third quarter 10-Q on the figures checked (net revenue 218,057 on page:7 of the release and page:4 of the 10-Q; cash and cash equivalents 81,085 on page:9 of the release and page:4 of the 10-Q; long-term debt 164,062 on both). The strongest contrary evidence is on the financing side. The credit agreement, its three amendments and the security agreement are exhibits incorporated by reference and are not in the pack (10-K page:131; third quarter 10-Q page:65), so every covenant, basket, guarantor and collateral statement rests on the issuer's own note summaries. Those summaries differ between filings: the second quarter 10-Q describes the liquidity covenant two ways (page:23, page:60), the springing secured net leverage test appears in the 10-K and the first two quarterly reports but not in the third quarter note, and the third quarter MD&A states the revolver at its post-amendment size while reporting borrowings at quarter end (page:60). The Silicon Motion arbitration has no quantified exposure (page:38). Consequence: CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5 can run as READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS, and the limits must be carried into each handoff; CP-2 must not present covenant headroom as verified against the executed agreement. The next evidence action is to obtain the executed credit agreement with Amendments No. 1 to No. 3 and the 8-K filed 2026-10-22 that carries the third amendment, and any filing between 2026-10-22 and 2026-11-05.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: MaxLinear is a single-entity, fabless semiconductor credit whose reported earnings inflected in 2026 while its balance sheet absorbed the growth. facts.label: Evidence, risk mechanism and credit implication
facts.text: 1. Earnings recovery is steep but short. Evidence: operating income of negative 17,209, negative 4,185 and 30,227 in Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026; trailing EBITDA proxy turns from negative 41,514 at Q2 to 29,865 at Q3. Risk mechanism: leverage and coverage ratios are driven by a single quarter, so a demand pause or margin slip reverses them. Implication: gross leverage of 5.52x exceeds the 3.50x covenant level, but the covenant is on net leverage (2.81x on the proxy), so compliance depends on cash netting and on the agreement's unsupplied EBITDA definition. 2. Growth consumes cash. Evidence: the nine-month cash flow statement shows cash absorbed of 27,259 by receivables, 35,618 by inventory and 68,168 by prepaid expenses and other assets (page:6); purchase obligations rose to 272,967. Risk mechanism: wafer prepayments and committed purchases precede revenue, so each step-up in the outlook needs financing before cash returns. Implication: revolver reliance rises with growth; availability, not earnings, is the binding constraint. 3. Single-bank secured structure with a 2028 wall. Evidence: 165,000 of principal, all maturing in 2028, floating rate at about 7.0% effective. Risk mechanism: no staggered maturities and a springing-test ambiguity. Implication: refinancing risk is concentrated in the first half of 2028 and the covenant package should be confirmed from the executed agreement. 4. Contingent claims are unsized. Evidence: the arbitration seeks the termination fee plus additional damages and costs; no loss is accrued. Risk mechanism: an award or settlement would be a cash outflow that reduces the unrestricted cash counted in the liquidity covenant. Implication: headroom analysis must be stressed for an unsized claim.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: MaxLinear, Inc. is a Delaware, Carlsbad-headquartered fabless designer of communications systems-on-chip that sells through distributors, module makers, original equipment manufacturers and original design manufacturers, and it is publicly held with no sponsor, parent or controlling holder disclosed in the sources (45 record holders and about 34,000 beneficial holders at 2026-01-22). Its business is changing fast: infrastructure, mainly optical products for data centers, was 57% of Q3 2026 net revenue against 32% in Q3 2025, while broadband fell from 46% to 24% of the quarter's revenue. That change raises revenue and margin, but concentrates risk: the ten largest customers were 56% of nine-month 2026 revenue (65% in FY2025, when two customers were 28%), customers buy on purchase orders with no long-term commitments, shipments to Asia were 85% of nine-month 2026 revenue (Hong Kong 52% in Q3 2026), one supplier took 52% of Q3 2026 inventory purchases, and the company states it has curtailed business with certain customers in China because of export controls. The creditor-relevant transaction history is the terminated Silicon Motion merger of 2022 to 2023: the company paid a USD 18.3 million ticking fee when committed financing was terminated and now faces a confidential Singapore arbitration in which Silicon Motion seeks the termination fee, further damages and costs, plus stockholder suits in two courts and a derivative action. No amount is accrued or estimated, and the filings state that damages could require drawing all lines of credit. On the financing side the sources show a single secured bank structure that was extended and enlarged in 2026 (second amendment of 2026-04-22; third amendment of 2026-10-16, a subsequent event to the quarter) and no notes or new debt issues; the only other 2026 funding transactions are an USD 8.0 million sale of an interest in claims and a revolver draw of USD 40.0 million. Strongest contrary evidence: the filings are consistent and primary, but the facts that would test control and creditor treatment (proxy statement, executed credit agreement and amendments, customer identities, order backlog) are not supplied, so governance conclusions are limited to documented actions. Consequence: the business view supports a fast-growing but concentrated, order-driven semiconductor credit with an unresolved legal overhang; the monitoring posture should key on customer concentration, supplier prepayments and the Silicon Motion docket.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The terminated Silicon Motion merger is the defining transaction. On 2022-05-05 MaxLinear agreed to acquire Silicon Motion Technology Corporation, a Cayman Islands maker of NAND flash controllers, by statutory merger, with debt financing committed by Wells Fargo Bank and other lenders under a second amended and restated commitment letter dated 2022-10-24 (10-K page:157). MaxLinear terminated the agreement on 2023-07-26, stating it owed no break-up fee; Silicon Motion disputes the termination and filed a notice of arbitration with the Singapore International Arbitration Centre on 2023-10-05, seeking the termination fee, additional damages, fees and costs, in a confidential proceeding (third quarter 10-Q page:14, page:38). The financing commitments were terminated and the company paid Wells Fargo a ticking fee of USD 18.3 million in August 2023 (10-K page:158). Silicon Motion stockholders have sued MaxLinear and officers: a putative class action filed 2023-08-31, dismissed with prejudice on 2025-07-15 and on appeal to the Ninth Circuit with briefing completed on 2026-04-13; a second federal action filed 2024-06-13 by HBK funds in which all but one claim survived a motion to dismiss; and a third action filed by the same plaintiffs on 2026-05-14 in San Diego Superior Court alleging fraud and related claims; a derivative action filed 2025-02-12 is stayed (third quarter 10-Q page:38-page:41). The company accrues no loss, regards an unfavorable outcome as reasonably possible and says a reasonable range cannot be estimated (page:43). Its 10-K states that damages or settlement could be significant and could require drawing all existing lines of credit, and that financing on favorable terms may not be available (10-K page:37-page:38). This is an unresolved contingent claim, not a debt instrument.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The only debt documents are the June 23, 2021 Credit Agreement (Initial Term Loan, original USD 350.0 million, and a revolver) and its amendments: a benchmark replacement on 2023-06-29; the Second Amendment of 2026-04-22, which extended the revolver from 2026-06-23 to 2028-03-23, added USD 30 million of commitments and a USD 10.0 million letter of credit commitment, raised the revolver margin to 2.25% and set a total net leverage ceiling of 3.50 to 1.00 and a liquidity floor of USD 80.0 million; and the Third Amendment of 2026-10-16, a subsequent event after the quarter, which adds USD 70 million of commitments for a total of USD 200 million and lowers the liquidity floor to USD 60.0 million. Proceeds of the revolver finance working capital and general corporate purposes. No new notes or other debt issues appear in the sources. In nine months 2026 the company borrowed USD 60.0 million on the revolver and repaid USD 20.0 million, leaving USD 40.0 million drawn, and in March 2026 it sold an interest in certain claims for up to USD 10.0 million, receiving USD 8.0 million used to pay costs of those claims, recorded as a long-term liability (third quarter 10-Q page:24). Use of the revolver draw beyond working capital is not itemised; the cash flow statement points to wafer prepayments and inventory (page:62).

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: The fundamental credit view is constructive but low-conviction: MaxLinear has moved from losses to operating profit within three quarters on a mix shift toward data center products, carries only secured bank debt of 165,000 (USD 165.0 million) maturing in 2028, and shows ample covenant liquidity on reported inputs, yet the improvement is one quarter old, cash conversion is negative and the contingent claim from the terminated Silicon Motion merger is unsized. Evidence: net revenue of 218,057 and income from operations of 30,227 in Q3 2026 against an operating loss of 17,209 in Q1 2026; trailing EBITDA proxy of 29,865, so total debt to EBITDA of 5.52x, net debt to EBITDA of 2.81x and EBITDA to cash interest of 3.51x; nine-month operating cash flow of negative 17,653 and free cash flow of negative 32,688 (financial base). Risk mechanic: the ratios are carried by Q3 2026 alone (excluding that quarter the trailing EBITDA proxy would be negative 9,215), revenue is order-based with no long-term purchase commitments and the ten largest customers were 56% of nine-month 2026 revenue (business handoff), and growth requires wafer prepayments and committed purchases of 272,967 before cash returns. Credit implication: default risk in the next twelve months looks contained by cash of 81,085, an undrawn revolver of 90,000 at quarter end (pro forma 160,000 after the 2026-10-16 amendment) and a lower liquidity floor, but leverage tolerance, refinancing in 2028 and the unsized legal claim cannot be assessed with confidence until the covenant EBITDA definition, the executed agreement and an indicator of the Silicon Motion exposure are available. Confidence is Medium because the upstream business handoff rates this module READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS, not READY, which keeps it below High. The strongest contrary evidence to the constructive tone is the 2028 concentration of all maturities and the negative cash conversion; the strongest support is the speed and mix of the revenue shift and the covenant relief obtained in October 2026.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: First, the earnings inflection is real but unseasoned. Operating income moved from negative 17,209 in Q1 2026 to negative 4,185 in Q2 2026 and 30,227 in Q3 2026 while net revenue rose from 137,188 to 168,847 and 218,057, with gross margin of 58.7% in Q3 2026. The trailing EBITDA proxy was negative until the Q3 2026 window, which means the 5.52x gross and 2.81x net leverage and 3.51x coverage exist for one window only and are carried by one quarter. This is a documentary fact from the financial base; the sustainability judgment is an analyst interpretation.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Second, cash conversion lags profit and growth is financed by the revolver. Net cash from operating activities was negative 17,653 for nine months 2026, free cash flow negative 32,688, and the revolver went from undrawn at 2026-06-30 to 40,000 drawn at 2026-09-30; management attributes the working-capital use to wafer prepayments for data center demand. The mechanic is that supplier prepayments and committed purchases of 272,967 precede cash from the ramp, so each step up in the Q4 2026 revenue outlook (management language: 240 to 260 million) needs further financing before it returns cash. Implication for liquidity: availability, not earnings, is the binding constraint.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Third, the debt structure is simple but concentrated. Debt principal is the Initial Term Loan of 125,000 due 2028-06-23 and the revolver of 40,000 drawn due 2028-03-23, floating rate at about 7.0% effective, secured on substantially all assets, with no amortization and no bonds. The mechanic is a single refinancing window in the first half of 2028 for the whole structure; the implication is no near-term maturity wall but a refinancing exposure that will be priced on the then-trailing earnings and on whether the growth is sustained.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Fourth, covenant headroom is wide on liquidity and unverified on leverage. The liquidity covenant requires 80,000 of cash plus available undrawn commitments at 2026-09-30 and the amendment of 2026-10-16 lowered the floor to 60,000; reported inputs give 171,085 against 80,000, headroom of 91,085 (about USD 91.1 million) before letters of credit, and 241,085 against 60,000 pro forma. The total net leverage ceiling is 3.50 to 1.00; on the strict GAAP proxy net leverage is 2.81x, 0.69x below the ceiling, but the agreement's Consolidated EBITDA is not supplied and may be much higher, and the second quarter 10-Q wording of the liquidity covenant conflicts with the others. The implication is that compliance is stated by the issuer but the true cushion is unknown.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Fifth, business risk is concentrated and short-visibility. Infrastructure was 57% of Q3 2026 revenue against 32% a year earlier; the ten largest customers were 56% of nine-month 2026 revenue and 65% in FY2025; customers order without long-term commitments; one supplier took 52% of Q3 2026 inventory purchases; Hong Kong was 52% of Q3 2026 revenue; export controls have already curtailed some China business. The mechanic is fast revenue transmission from a design win or order pause into cash flow while R&D and people costs are fixed in the near term.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Sixth, the Silicon Motion claim is an unsized tail. The arbitration seeks the termination fee, additional damages, fees and costs; three stockholder suits are pending; no loss is accrued; the company states damages could be significant and could require drawing all lines of credit. On a strict-proxy basis a cash outflow of about 20,613 (USD 20.6 million) would take net leverage to the 3.50x ceiling, and the liquidity covenant would absorb about 91,085 before reaching its quarter-end floor (see Calculations); neither can be tested against a claim size because none is disclosed.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths are, first, the revenue and margin momentum in infrastructure products, where revenue rose from 40,343 to 124,907 year on year in Q3 and gross margin improved to 58.7% from 56.9%; second, liquidity that is ample on the covenant measure, with cash and equivalents of 81,085, undrawn revolver of 90,000, and lender support shown by the 2026-04-22 and 2026-10-16 amendments that extended the maturity, added 30 million then 70 million of commitments and lowered the floor from 80.0 to 60.0 million; third, a simple capital structure of bank debt only, with no amortization before 2028, and a modest historical cash interest bill of 8,508 over the trailing twelve months; fourth, an asset-light fabless model with capital purchases of 15,035 over nine months; and fifth, reporting quality, with effective internal control over financial reporting and prompt disclosure of the 2026 amendments.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses are, first, negative cash conversion, with nine-month operating cash flow of negative 17,653 and growth financed by the revolver; second, thin and new earnings, since the trailing EBITDA proxy of 29,865 is carried by Q3 2026, the trailing net loss is 29,372 and stock-based compensation of 86,923 over the trailing twelve months is a large non-cash charge relative to EBITDA; third, concentration in customers (the ten largest at 56% of nine-month 2026 revenue), in one inventory supplier (52% of Q3 2026 purchases), in ship-to geography (Asia 85% of nine-month 2026 revenue) and in an order basis with no long-term commitments; fourth, claims outside debt that are large relative to cash, notably purchase obligations of 272,967 and software and other obligations of 74,589; fifth, the unsized Silicon Motion exposure and related suits, whose count grew from two in the 10-K to three in the third quarter 10-Q; sixth, a single 2028 maturity for all debt at a floating rate of about 7.0%; and seventh, unverified covenant terms because the executed agreement, amendments and compliance certificate are not supplied.

Question answered: can the effective source set support the requested downstream work, and what remains blocked? This module gives no credit conclusion, legal interpretation or investment opinion, and it calculates and normalizes nothing.

### Financial base view

MaxLinear is a single-entity, fabless semiconductor credit whose reported earnings inflected in 2026 while its balance sheet absorbed the growth. Net revenue rose from 137,188 in Q1 2026 to 168,847 in Q2 2026 and 218,057 in Q3 2026 (first quarter 10-Q `page:2`-`page:3`; second quarter 10-Q `page:4`-`page:5`; third quarter 10-Q `page:4`-`page:5`). Income from operations moved from a loss of 17,209 in Q1 2026 to a profit of 30,227 in Q3 2026. On a GAAP EBITDA proxy that adds back depreciation and intangible amortization (not operating lease amortization, and not stock-based compensation), trailing twelve-month EBITDA to 2026-09-30 is 29,865, which gives total debt of 165,000 a ratio of 5.52x and net debt of 83,915 a ratio of 2.81x; trailing EBITDA coverage of cash interest is 3.51x. Those ratios exist only for the latest window: the proxy was negative for FY2024, FY2025 and the trailing windows to Q1 2026 and Q2 2026, and excluding Q3 2026 the trailing figure would be negative 9,215. The strongest contrary evidence is cash: net cash used in operating activities was 17,653 for nine months 2026 (about USD 17.7 million), against 9,213 provided in nine months 2025, because receivables, inventory and prepaid expenses absorbed cash (`page:6` of the third quarter 10-Q; management attributes it to wafer prepayments and inventory for data center demand, `page:62`). The revolver went from undrawn at 2026-06-30 to 40,000 drawn at 2026-09-30, and total debt principal rose from 125,000 to 165,000. Definition risks run both ways: the proxy is far below what the credit agreement's Consolidated EBITDA might show (stock-based compensation alone was 86,923 over the trailing twelve months), but that definition is not supplied, so covenant compliance, which the issuer states as met at 2026-09-30 (`page:24`), cannot be verified. In USD millions the headline figures are: Q3 2026 net revenue USD 218.1 million; Q3 2026 income from operations USD 30.2 million; nine-month 2026 operating cash flow negative USD 17.7 million; total debt principal USD 165.0 million, being the term loan of USD 125.0 million plus the revolver draw of USD 40.0 million; undrawn revolver USD 90.0 million at 2026-09-30; inventory purchase obligations USD 273.0 million; and a liquidity covenant floor of USD 80.0 million that the amendment of 2026-10-16 lowers to USD 60.0 million. Consequence for the credit view: operating momentum is real and the covenant package looks accommodating, but leverage depends on one quarter, cash conversion is negative, working-capital commitments are still growing, and all debt matures in 2028.

1. Earnings recovery is steep but short. Evidence: operating income of negative 17,209, negative 4,185 and 30,227 in Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026; trailing EBITDA proxy turns from negative 41,514 at Q2 to 29,865 at Q3. Risk mechanism: leverage and coverage ratios are driven by a single quarter, so a demand pause or margin slip reverses them. Implication: gross leverage of 5.52x exceeds the 3.50x covenant level, but the covenant is on net leverage (2.81x on the proxy), so compliance depends on cash netting and on the agreement's unsupplied EBITDA definition.

2. Growth consumes cash. Risk mechanism: wafer prepayments and committed purchases precede revenue, so each step-up in the outlook needs financing before cash returns. Implication: revolver reliance rises with growth; availability, not earnings, is the binding constraint.

3. Single-bank secured structure with a 2028 wall. Evidence: 165,000 of principal, all maturing in 2028, floating rate at about 7.0% effective. Risk mechanism: no staggered maturities and a springing-test ambiguity. Implication: refinancing risk is concentrated in the first half of 2028 and the covenant package should be confirmed from the executed agreement.

4. Contingent claims are unsized. Evidence: the arbitration seeks the termination fee plus additional damages and costs; no loss is accrued. Risk mechanism: an award or settlement would be a cash outflow that reduces the unrestricted cash counted in the liquidity covenant. Implication: headroom analysis must be stressed for an unsized claim.

## Findings
### Reader summary

### Business and transaction view

MaxLinear, Inc. is a Delaware, Carlsbad-headquartered fabless designer of communications systems-on-chip that sells through distributors, module makers, original equipment manufacturers and original design manufacturers, and it is publicly held with no sponsor, parent or controlling holder disclosed in the sources (45 record holders and about 34,000 beneficial holders at 2026-01-22). Its business is changing fast: infrastructure, mainly optical products for data centers, was 57% of Q3 2026 net revenue against 32% in Q3 2025, while broadband fell from 46% to 24% of the quarter's revenue. That change raises revenue and margin, but concentrates risk: the ten largest customers were 56% of nine-month 2026 revenue (65% in FY2025, when two customers were 28%), customers buy on purchase orders with no long-term commitments, shipments to Asia were 85% of nine-month 2026 revenue (Hong Kong 52% in Q3 2026), one supplier took 52% of Q3 2026 inventory purchases, and the company states it has curtailed business with certain customers in China because of export controls. The creditor-relevant transaction history is the terminated Silicon Motion merger of 2022 to 2023: the company paid a USD 18.3 million ticking fee when committed financing was terminated and now faces a confidential Singapore arbitration in which Silicon Motion seeks the termination fee, further damages and costs, plus stockholder suits in two courts and a derivative action. No amount is accrued or estimated, and the filings state that damages could require drawing all lines of credit. On the financing side the sources show a single secured bank structure that was extended and enlarged in 2026 (second amendment of 2026-04-22; third amendment of 2026-10-16, a subsequent event to the quarter) and no notes or new debt issues; the only other 2026 funding transactions are an USD 8.0 million sale of an interest in claims and a revolver draw of USD 40.0 million. Strongest contrary evidence: the filings are consistent and primary, but the facts that would test control and creditor treatment (proxy statement, executed credit agreement and amendments, customer identities, order backlog) are not supplied, so governance conclusions are limited to documented actions. ### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The terminated Silicon Motion merger is the defining transaction. On 2022-05-05 MaxLinear agreed to acquire Silicon Motion Technology Corporation, a Cayman Islands maker of NAND flash controllers, by statutory merger, with debt financing committed by Wells Fargo Bank and other lenders under a second amended and restated commitment letter dated 2022-10-24 (10-K `page:157`). MaxLinear terminated the agreement on 2023-07-26, stating it owed no break-up fee; Silicon Motion disputes the termination and filed a notice of arbitration with the Singapore International Arbitration Centre on 2023-10-05, seeking the termination fee, additional damages, fees and costs, in a confidential proceeding (third quarter 10-Q `page:14`, `page:38`). The financing commitments were terminated and the company paid Wells Fargo a ticking fee of USD 18.3 million in August 2023 (10-K `page:158`). Silicon Motion stockholders have sued MaxLinear and officers: a putative class action filed 2023-08-31, dismissed with prejudice on 2025-07-15 and on appeal to the Ninth Circuit with briefing completed on 2026-04-13; a second federal action filed 2024-06-13 by HBK funds in which all but one claim survived a motion to dismiss; and a third action filed by the same plaintiffs on 2026-05-14 in San Diego Superior Court alleging fraud and related claims; a derivative action filed 2025-02-12 is stayed (third quarter 10-Q `page:38`-`page:41`). The company accrues no loss, regards an unfavorable outcome as reasonably possible and says a reasonable range cannot be estimated (`page:43`). Its 10-K states that damages or settlement could be significant and could require drawing all existing lines of credit, and that financing on favorable terms may not be available (10-K `page:37`-`page:38`). This is an unresolved contingent claim, not a debt instrument.

The only debt documents are the June 23, 2021 Credit Agreement (Initial Term Loan, original USD 350.0 million, and a revolver) and its amendments: a benchmark replacement on 2023-06-29; the Second Amendment of 2026-04-22, which extended the revolver from 2026-06-23 to 2028-03-23, added USD 30 million of commitments and a USD 10.0 million letter of credit commitment, raised the revolver margin to 2.25% and set a total net leverage ceiling of 3.50 to 1.00 and a liquidity floor of USD 80.0 million; and the Third Amendment of 2026-10-16, a subsequent event after the quarter, which adds USD 70 million of commitments for a total of USD 200 million and lowers the liquidity floor to USD 60.0 million. Proceeds of the revolver finance working capital and general corporate purposes. No new notes or other debt issues appear in the sources. In nine months 2026 the company borrowed USD 60.0 million on the revolver and repaid USD 20.0 million, leaving USD 40.0 million drawn, and in March 2026 it sold an interest in certain claims for up to USD 10.0 million, receiving USD 8.0 million used to pay costs of those claims, recorded as a long-term liability (third quarter 10-Q `page:24`). Use of the revolver draw beyond working capital is not itemised; the cash flow statement points to wafer prepayments and inventory (`page:62`).

Other transactions: a USD 2.0 million convertible note receivable from a privately-held entity (2026-01-05, 3.87% interest, due 2029-01-05) and the supplier note receivable above (third quarter 10-Q `page:18`); a contingent consideration of USD 2.6 million from an acquisition in January 2023, unpaid pending resolution of certain matters (`page:17`); a share repurchase program of up to USD 75.0 million authorized on 2025-11-20, under which USD 20.0 million was repurchased in 2025 and none in nine months 2026, leaving about USD 55.0 million available (`page:44`). The executed credit agreement, amendments and the filing that carries the Third Amendment are not supplied; terms above are the issuer's summaries.

Module: fundamental credit synthesis for MAXLINEAR, INC (MaxLinear, Inc., Nasdaq: MXL, issuer id mxl), as of 2026-11-05, evidence cutoff 2026-11-05. Pathway: credit snapshot; reporting currency USD, amounts in thousands unless a label says millions; current period q3-2026 (quarter and nine months to 2026-09-30), prior period fy-2025. Reader question: what is the fundamental credit view, and which strengths, weaknesses, findings and risks drive it. Required drivers: business risk (from the business and transaction handoff), financial risk and liquidity (from the financial base handoff), and the gaps that limit both. The evidence is upstream only: every conclusion rests on the named sections of the three supplied handoffs, whose figures are reused unchanged, and the issuer sources are listed because the handoffs rest on them. This module compares the issuer with no peers, expresses no view on any instrument and reaches no conclusion on loss outcomes; relative value and security selection are outside it. Each assessment row carries one tag: Documentary Fact, Management Language, Analyst Interpretation or Insufficient Information.
## Sources

Run context (not issuer evidence): context, sha256 39695f94e05534dbaa55be69eaec116e2e3f550f0af980e236d8132f5e5386f2.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Business momentum has improved sharply, but the credit is unseasoned: trailing leverage is 5.52x gross and 2.81x net on a GAAP EBITDA proxy, cash conversion is negative, and an unsized legal claim and 2028 maturities remain. | Medium | The credit agreement's EBITDA definition and the Silicon Motion exposure are not supplied, so covenant headroom and downside cannot be verified. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Earnings turned positive only in the latest quarter, so trailing leverage and the coverage of 3.51x rest on one quarter. | Small shifts in demand or margin could reverse coverage and leverage quickly. | Medium |
| Nine-month operating cash flow was negative and the revolver funded growth. | Liquidity, not earnings, is the binding constraint, so availability and borrowing conditions matter most. | High |
| All debt, USD 165.0 million, matures in 2028 on a floating-rate secured structure with no amortization. | There is no near-term maturity wall, but one refinancing window in 2028. | High |

| Covenant liquidity headroom is large on reported inputs, but leverage headroom depends on an unsupplied EBITDA definition. | A payment of about USD 20.6 million would reach the 3.50x ceiling on the strict proxy, and far more on a broader definition. | Medium |
| The Silicon Motion arbitration and related suits are unquantified. | A tail claim on liquidity that cannot be sized from the sources. | Low |
### Credit view

The fundamental credit view is constructive but low-conviction: MaxLinear has moved from losses to operating profit within three quarters on a mix shift toward data center products, carries only secured bank debt of 165,000 (USD 165.0 million) maturing in 2028, and shows ample covenant liquidity on reported inputs, yet the improvement is one quarter old, cash conversion is negative and the contingent claim from the terminated Silicon Motion merger is unsized. Evidence: net revenue of 218,057 and income from operations of 30,227 in Q3 2026 against an operating loss of 17,209 in Q1 2026; trailing EBITDA proxy of 29,865, so total debt to EBITDA of 5.52x, net debt to EBITDA of 2.81x and EBITDA to cash interest of 3.51x; nine-month operating cash flow of negative 17,653 and free cash flow of negative 32,688 (financial base). Risk mechanic: the ratios are carried by Q3 2026 alone (excluding that quarter the trailing EBITDA proxy would be negative 9,215), revenue is order-based with no long-term purchase commitments and the ten largest customers were 56% of nine-month 2026 revenue (business handoff), and growth requires wafer prepayments and committed purchases of 272,967 before cash returns. Credit implication: default risk in the next twelve months looks contained by cash of 81,085, an undrawn revolver of 90,000 at quarter end (pro forma 160,000 after the 2026-10-16 amendment) and a lower liquidity floor, but leverage tolerance, refinancing in 2028 and the unsized legal claim cannot be assessed with confidence until the covenant EBITDA definition, the executed agreement and an indicator of the Silicon Motion exposure are available. Confidence is Medium because the upstream business handoff rates this module READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS, not READY, which keeps it below High. The strongest contrary evidence to the constructive tone is the 2028 concentration of all maturities and the negative cash conversion; the strongest support is the speed and mix of the revenue shift and the covenant relief obtained in October 2026.
### Key findings

First, the earnings inflection is real but unseasoned. Operating income moved from negative 17,209 in Q1 2026 to negative 4,185 in Q2 2026 and 30,227 in Q3 2026 while net revenue rose from 137,188 to 168,847 and 218,057, with gross margin of 58.7% in Q3 2026. The trailing EBITDA proxy was negative until the Q3 2026 window, which means the 5.52x gross and 2.81x net leverage and 3.51x coverage exist for one window only and are carried by one quarter. This is a documentary fact from the financial base; the sustainability judgment is an analyst interpretation.

Second, cash conversion lags profit and growth is financed by the revolver. Net cash from operating activities was negative 17,653 for nine months 2026, free cash flow negative 32,688, and the revolver went from undrawn at 2026-06-30 to 40,000 drawn at 2026-09-30; management attributes the working-capital use to wafer prepayments for data center demand. The mechanic is that supplier prepayments and committed purchases of 272,967 precede cash from the ramp, so each step up in the Q4 2026 revenue outlook (management language: 240 to 260 million) needs further financing before it returns cash. Implication for liquidity: availability, not earnings, is the binding constraint.

Third, the debt structure is simple but concentrated. Debt principal is the Initial Term Loan of 125,000 due 2028-06-23 and the revolver of 40,000 drawn due 2028-03-23, floating rate at about 7.0% effective, secured on substantially all assets, with no amortization and no bonds. The mechanic is a single refinancing window in the first half of 2028 for the whole structure; the implication is no near-term maturity wall but a refinancing exposure that will be priced on the then-trailing earnings and on whether the growth is sustained.

Fourth, covenant headroom is wide on liquidity and unverified on leverage. The liquidity covenant requires 80,000 of cash plus available undrawn commitments at 2026-09-30 and the amendment of 2026-10-16 lowered the floor to 60,000; reported inputs give 171,085 against 80,000, headroom of 91,085 (about USD 91.1 million) before letters of credit, and 241,085 against 60,000 pro forma. The total net leverage ceiling is 3.50 to 1.00; on the strict GAAP proxy net leverage is 2.81x, 0.69x below the ceiling, but the agreement's Consolidated EBITDA is not supplied and may be much higher, and the second quarter 10-Q wording of the liquidity covenant conflicts with the others. The implication is that compliance is stated by the issuer but the true cushion is unknown.

Fifth, business risk is concentrated and short-visibility. Infrastructure was 57% of Q3 2026 revenue against 32% a year earlier; the ten largest customers were 56% of nine-month 2026 revenue and 65% in FY2025; customers order without long-term commitments; one supplier took 52% of Q3 2026 inventory purchases; Hong Kong was 52% of Q3 2026 revenue; export controls have already curtailed some China business. The mechanic is fast revenue transmission from a design win or order pause into cash flow while R&D and people costs are fixed in the near term.

Sixth, the Silicon Motion claim is an unsized tail. The arbitration seeks the termination fee, additional damages, fees and costs; three stockholder suits are pending; no loss is accrued; the company states damages could be significant and could require drawing all lines of credit. On a strict-proxy basis a cash outflow of about 20,613 (USD 20.6 million) would take net leverage to the 3.50x ceiling, and the liquidity covenant would absorb about 91,085 before reaching its quarter-end floor (see Calculations); neither can be tested against a claim size because none is disclosed.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths are, first, the revenue and margin momentum in infrastructure products, where revenue rose from 40,343 to 124,907 year on year in Q3 and gross margin improved to 58.7% from 56.9%; second, liquidity that is ample on the covenant measure, with cash and equivalents of 81,085, undrawn revolver of 90,000, and lender support shown by the 2026-04-22 and 2026-10-16 amendments that extended the maturity, added 30 million then 70 million of commitments and lowered the floor from 80.0 to 60.0 million; third, a simple capital structure of bank debt only, with no amortization before 2028, and a modest historical cash interest bill of 8,508 over the trailing twelve months; fourth, an asset-light fabless model with capital purchases of 15,035 over nine months; and fifth, reporting quality, with effective internal control over financial reporting and prompt disclosure of the 2026 amendments.

Weaknesses are, first, negative cash conversion, with nine-month operating cash flow of negative 17,653 and growth financed by the revolver; second, thin and new earnings, since the trailing EBITDA proxy of 29,865 is carried by Q3 2026, the trailing net loss is 29,372 and stock-based compensation of 86,923 over the trailing twelve months is a large non-cash charge relative to EBITDA; third, concentration in customers (the ten largest at 56% of nine-month 2026 revenue), in one inventory supplier (52% of Q3 2026 purchases), in ship-to geography (Asia 85% of nine-month 2026 revenue) and in an order basis with no long-term commitments; fourth, claims outside debt that are large relative to cash, notably purchase obligations of 272,967 and software and other obligations of 74,589; fifth, the unsized Silicon Motion exposure and related suits, whose count grew from two in the 10-K to three in the third quarter 10-Q; sixth, a single 2028 maturity for all debt at a floating rate of about 7.0%; and seventh, unverified covenant terms because the executed agreement, amendments and compliance certificate are not supplied.
